ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and beneficial owners against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council sanctions implemented through Global Affairs Canada, and Canadian domestic sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. FINTRAC-compliant customer due diligence requires identification verification, source of funds/source of wealth assessment, and adverse media checks. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any underlying owner is a foreign politically exposed person (PEP).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Online Services, including Corporate Online at corporateonline.gov.bc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must contain a permitted legal element, such as 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', or a recognized equivalent. Names may be submitted in English or French; non-Latin script trade names must include a Romanized transliteration or an English/French translation. The Registrar reviews distinctiveness, confusion, prohibited terms, and public policy compliance. The legal element may not be translated into a foreign language for the official corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A BC Name Request is valid for 56 days. Extensions are not issued upon lapse; the applicant must file a new Name Request and pay the applicable fee. If the name is refused, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of refusal, including a full legal and commercial justification and a comparative list of existing names supporting distinguishability. If the reconsideration is denied, judicial review can be sought before the Supreme Court of British Columbia using the judicial review procedure under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c 241.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered agent's physical street address in British Columbia is permissible for the registered office and records office, provided it is a real, staffed location at which service of legal process and correspondence can be received, and it is not a mere post office box or virtual cloud-only address. For the wholesale export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, no additional statutory requirement mandating a physical operational office is triggered, though the company must maintain proper accounting records and a registered agent capable of receiving process in BC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximate annual probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection is less than 5% for a low-risk wholesale herbal commodity exporter operating through a BC ULC, absent a specific CRA tax audit, FINTRAC criminal referral, or a regulatory search warrant relating to the Import/Export Act or the Safe Food for Canadians Act. Routine compliance inspections are documentary and may be served at the registered office rather than at a physical operations site.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c 56, ss 10, 21, 22, 165, 177; applicable BC corporate Forms and Notices; Notice of Articles Regulation made thereunder.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) together with Incorporation Agreement, submitted through BC Corporate Online or by paper filing
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a BC Unlimited Liability Corporation; no escrow or capital deposit account is required by the Business Corporations Act. Shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine, and paid-up capital for income tax purposes is computed separately under the Income Tax Act (Canada).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the incorporator has submitted the Incorporation Agreement and Notice of Articles for an Unlimited Liability Corporation; BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The share subscription tendered by the subscriber is accepted, and the President is directed to allot one (1) Class A Unlimited Voting Common Share against payment of the agreed subscription price. 2. The registered office in British Columbia set out in the Notice of Articles is adopted, and the President shall maintain and file any required notice of change. 3. [Name] is appointed President and Secretary, and [Name2] is appointed director to hold office as permitted by statute. 4. The directors are authorized to open banking accounts and adopt the interim bylaws of the Corporation. DATED [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services – Name Approval system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Request through the BC corporate online platform, providing up to three proposed corporate names. The name must be distinct, consistent with the BC ULC naming rules, and must not cause confusion with existing corporate or registered trade names.
required_dossiers: Proposed ULC corporate name (up to three alternatives)
Name Request fee
Consent of any person or entity whose name is used in the proposed corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name request is queried or rejected, resubmit revised name preferences or provide written justification relying on distinctiveness, together with any supporting consents, to BC Registries for reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Incorporation Agreement and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator's legal representative; forms governed by the BC Business Corporations Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Notice of Articles containing the registered office address, first directors, share structure, any special rights or restrictions attached to shares, and the statement that the corporation is an Unlimited Liability Corporation. Prepare and execute the Incorporation Agreement confirming the subscriber's intent to form the corporation.
required_dossiers: Completed Notice of Articles (Form 1)
Incorporation Agreement executed by incorporator
Consent of first director
Consent to act as registered office address (if not the corporation's own premises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registry staff identify incompleteness or technical defects, amend the affected form and resubmit; if the defect is substantive, a fresh consent or director signature may be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Filing and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services – BC Corporate Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the BC Corporate Online service, enter the Notice of Articles data, attach the Incorporation Agreement, and remit the registry filing fee by credit card. Verify that the corporation type is recorded as an Unlimited Liability Corporation and that all signatures are properly authorized.
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation or name request number
Final Notice of Articles data
Incorporation Agreement in electronic or scanned form
Credit card payment authorization for registry fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected because of a statutory deficiency, the BC Registry will issue a deficiency notice; cure by submitting the corrected document or paying any shortfall within the stated response period, failing which the application may be abandoned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Records Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and the official Notice of Articles from the corporate registry. Create a corporate records book containing the certificate, Notice of Articles, resolutions, share register, directors register, and registered office records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by BC Registries
Certified Notice of Articles
Corporate records book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated due to system error or data mismatch, contact BC Registries Client Support and request a certified copy or corrected certificate; provide the assigned BC company number and filing confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and Federal Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number using the Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles. Register for the GST/HST account if the corporation supplies taxable supplies in Canada and is not a small supplier; register for the Import/Export Program account if goods will be imported or exported as part of the dried goji berry operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Notice of Articles
Director and officer names, addresses, and social insurance or business identification information
Principal business activity description under ISIC 4631 / NAICS 424490
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the registration, respond to the compliance questionnaire, confirm the transition of control rules applicable to a ULC, and provide the required supporting corporate documents to establish GST registration requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Ministry of Finance – Provincial Tax and Revenue Administration (PTRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC through eTaxBC for provincial tax accounts. Register for a BC PST account if the corporation will make taxable sales in British Columbia; dried food products may be PST-exempt, but registration is recommended to document exempt sales. Review BC Employer Health Tax obligations if payroll thresholds are met.
required_dossiers: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number
BC company number and Notice of Articles
Estimated BC payroll and revenue information
Description of wholesale distribution activities and product nature
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the PTRA denies or delays account issuance, contact the Provincial Tax Registration Desk, clarify product taxability with an exemption certificate, and provide the governing corporate documents supporting passive wholesale activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupancy Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City, District, or Regional District Business Licensing Department where the registered office or warehouse is situated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence authorizing wholesale warehousing and distribution of dried botanical food products. Obtain any necessary occupancy permit for the premises, confirm compliance with zoning for warehouse use, and complete a fire and building safety inspection before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Notice of Articles
Lease or proof of ownership of the operating premises
Municipal business licence application
Site floor plan and building occupancy classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues a deficiency relating to zoning or occupancy, submit a building permit application for change of use, coordinate with the local fire department, and request a temporary business licence pending final inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Good Standing and Annual Compliance Calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries, Canada Revenue Agency, and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the BC Annual Report within the statutory period following each anniversary of incorporation, pay the required annual report fee, maintain the corporate records at the registered office, and satisfy any CRA and WorkSafeBC annual return or payroll filing obligations.
required_dossiers: Annual report filing data
Certification of directors and officers as of the annual date
Financial statement information if required under the Business Corporations Act
Proof of registered office maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual report or tax return is filed late, pay the applicable late-filing penalty and reinstatement fee; if the company is struck or dissolved, apply for restoration under the Business Corporations Act within the permitted restoration period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) – Safe Food for Canadians Program
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act Licence – Food Business Wholesale and International Export (Dried Goji Berries and Herbal Botanicals)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy; Environmental Assessment Office; municipal sewer and stormwater authorities where applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no mandatory Environmental Assessment Certificate for a wholesale and export warehouse operation under the BC Environmental Assessment Act; administrative registration or municipal environmental permits may apply where repackaging or material handling occurs.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater is anticipated; any wash-down water must comply with municipal sewer use bylaws under the BC Municipal Sewerage Regulation and the Environmental Management Act. Stormwater discharge must meet the applicable municipal stormwater control bylaw. VOC emissions are not expected from raw dried botanicals, but any alcohol-based herbal tincture handling would be subject to the VOC Concentration Limits for Certain Products Regulation (Canada).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Standing fire safety certification under the BC Fire Code; municipal building occupancy inspection and structural load clearance for palletized storage; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety registration and clearance for warehouse operations, including manual handling, forklift use, and sanitation protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – GST/HST and corporate income tax administration; BC Ministry of Finance for provincial PST; CRA portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity intending to carry on business in Canada or deriving taxable Canadian-source income must obtain a Business Number (BN) from the CRA. Registration is completed via the CRA’s Business Registration Online (BRO) service, by mail using Form RC1, or through a registered tax service provider. The BC Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) must be registered under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act, after which the CRA assigns a BN with a corporate income tax program account (RC0001), a GST/HST program account (RT0001), and a payroll program account (RP0001) where applicable. A non-resident entity may also need a deemed BN for GST/HST registration if it supplies taxable supplies in Canada and is not exempt under the de minimis threshold. Supporting documents include: certificate of incorporation, articles, registered office address, directors’ information, and proof of non-resident status (e.g., Form NR301 for treaty-based withholding exemptions where relevant).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A BC ULC is a limited liability company under provincial law but, for Canadian income tax purposes, it is a taxable Canadian corporation unless a valid election under the Income Tax Act applies. Cross-border hybrid mismatch planning is constrained by Canada’s hybrid mismatch rules (sections 12.4, 18.15, 18.16, 20.1 and related provisions). For U.S. federal tax purposes, the ULC may be treated as a disregarded entity under the U.S. 'check-the-box' classification election (Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3), provided it is not per se a corporation. Canada may recharacterize the entity under treaty or domestic law, creating potential hybrid entity mismatches. The taxpayer should consider filing Form 8832 (U.S. check-the-box) and Canadian disclosure forms (e.g., Form RC4640, Form T106 for foreign affiliate transactions) to align classification and mitigate double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) plus provincial sales taxes where applicable; BC has no provincial GST/HST analogue but applies PST on specified taxable supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in global gross revenue from taxable supplies (other than zero-rated supplies) over any of the calendar quarters in the immediately preceding four quarters; registration is mandatory once threshold is exceeded, and voluntary registration is available. For a non-resident ULC, registration is also required if it solicits orders or supplies in Canada and does not meet the small-supplier threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time e-invoicing or fiscal clearance through an API-connected tax server. GST/HST-compliant invoices must contain: supplier’s name or trading name, BN, invoice date, a clear description of goods or services, and GST/HST amount. A QR code or digital stamp is not required. However, all invoices and supporting export records must be maintained in electronic or paper form for six years, and CRA may request digital access in prescribed formats during audit. A ULC exporting commercial quantities of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals should implement a robust electronic records system capable of producing line-item reconciliations, proof of export, and FX repatriation evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible personal property (including dried goji berries and herbal botanicals sold in international bulk wholesale transactions) are zero-rated under Section 1, Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, provided the vendor sells and delivers the goods to the purchaser for full export and the goods are physically exported from Canada without further manufacturing, processing, or repackaging in Canada prior to export. Zero-rating also requires the supplier to maintain evidence establishing export within a reasonable time (usually within 60 days or as commercially reasonable) and that the goods leave Canada. Offshore supply of services and intangible personal property connected to the export contract may be zero-rated under Part V, Schedule VII, subject to place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Exporter Declaration / G13, CAED) or equivalent CBSA-approved export reporting, including the Customs Entry Number (E-number) where applicable
Commercial Invoice, clearly marked 'Dried Goji Berries / Lycium barbarum', tariff classification under HS 1211 or HS 0813 (dried fruit), quantity, and unit price
Packing List / Weighted Shelf Report detailing pallet/box counts, net and gross weights
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing the shipment leave Canada
Export Cargo Report or carrier confirmation issued by the customs broker, freight forwarder, or carrier
Proof of payment (bank transfer instruction, SWIFT MT103) showing the foreign buyer remits funds
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank acknowledgement of FX purchase / international wire credited to the Canadian exporter’s bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits export zero-rating claims with a high degree of scrutiny. A false or unsupported zero-rating claim results in reassessment of GST/HST at 5%, plus arrears interest and owing penalties. Negligence or knowingly making a false statement triggers a penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 or 50% of the understated net tax under subsection 280(1) of the Excise Tax Act. Criminal or civil fraud exposure may arise under section 327 or 328 of the Excise Tax Act and section 380 of the Criminal Code, with fines of up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment for up to two years for summary conviction. Retrospective clawbacks are available for up to seven years from the filing date, and the CRA may deny the zero-rating permanently if export documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, or includes fraud indicators.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority, with FX policy administered jointly by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), and Global Affairs Canada under the Export and Import Permits Act (EIPA). No dedicated foreign exchange administration agency exists; Canada maintains a market-based floating currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates under a fully liberalized, free-floating exchange-rate regime with no exchange-control statute. Both current-account items (trade settlement, freight, royalties) and capital-account items (equity injection, intercompany loans, shareholder dividends) are freely convertible and transferable. Profit remittance by a non-resident shareholder of a BC ULC is unrestricted from a banking/FX standpoint, subject only to Part XIII withholding tax on outbound dividends. The Investment Canada Act imposes no review on the organic formation of a ULC; review would arise only upon acquisition of control of an existing Canadian business. Dried Lycium and herbal botanicals are standard commodities requiring no specialized capital-account permit, but exports are subject to CFIA inspection and Canadian Food Inspection Agency export attestation; neither creates convertibility obstacles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline apply to Canadian export receipts. A BC ULC may hold export proceeds indefinitely in USD or CNY foreign-currency accounts with a Schedule I bank. The only reporting duty is the electronic B13A export declaration under s.95 of the Customs Act for shipments valued over CAD 2,000. Dried Lycium barbarum (HS 1211.90) is not on the Export Control List, so no EIPA export permit is required absent sanctions or controlled-goods triggers.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium (auxiliary treasury only). Offshore digital EMI platforms (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) operate in Canada as money-services businesses under the PCMLTFA and must hold FINTRAC MSB registration; payment functions also require Bank of Canada registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act effective November 2024. Such EMIs cannot lawfully use the 'bank' descriptor under the Bank Act, cannot hold statutory capital escrow for a ULC, cannot issue commercial letters of credit, and provide no CDIC deposit insurance. Their utility is limited to low-value operational receivable collection and supplier disbursements; all primary clearing must run through a regulated Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canada's major banks generally mandate an in-person onboarding interview for at least one authorized signatory/director at a BC branch, particularly where a 25% or greater beneficial owner is a non-resident. Remote account opening is legally permissible under FINTRAC's dual-process verification rule, requiring (i) notarized government-issued identification and (ii) an independent source such as a registered agent or professional accountant; banks nevertheless escalate remote applications for enhanced review (2-4 weeks). A non-resident director may delegate execution powers to a Canadian lawyer under an irrevocable power of attorney in lieu of physical attendance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the ULC, triggering FINTRAC beneficial-ownership identification obligations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport and recent proof of address; British Columbia corporate registry extract; signed beneficial-ownership declaration; notarized source-of-wealth letter; three months of prime-bank statements and a professional (lawyer/CPA) reference confirming legitimacy of accumulated funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited Liability Corporation pass-through classification perceived as an opaque or unusual structure by credit-risk officers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate organizational chart; certified copy of the BC Business Corporations Act unlimited-liability election; legal opinion confirming that unlimited liability attaches only to shareholders and does not create veil-piercing exposure for the bank; officer's certificate describing the ULC's US check-the-box tax treatment rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Repeated high-value wires to China/Hong Kong for herbal raw-material settlement with third-party suppliers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master supply agreements with named growers; commercial invoices and pro-forma contracts; phytosanitary certificates and Canada Organic Regime (COR) attestation; bills of lading and forwarder booking confirmations; narrative purpose statement consistent with the entity's low-risk wholesale trading profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large one-off inbound equity injection from a foreign corporate shareholder into the capital escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share-subscription resolution and board minutes; bank statements of the subscribing corporate shareholder for the source of funds; intercompany agreement describing the ULC equity structure; tax registration certificate; and sworn source-of-funds declaration on the form prescribed by the receiving institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route via SWIFT MT103 from the subscribing shareholder's bank to the ULC's escrow account at a Schedule I bank in Vancouver. Field 50K must name the remitting shareholder; field 70 must state 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION – ULC SHARE ISSUANCE'; attach the executed subscription agreement, board resolution, and source-of-funds evidence. For wires exceeding CAD 100,000, deliver a sworn source-of-funds declaration in advance. Canada does not require a national mandatory purpose-code registry; use the OECD classification '1100 – Direct Investment, Equity' in remittance narratives. The receiving bank will verify the corporate registry, confirm the shareholder's identity, and reconcile the incoming payment against the escrow account mandate before releasing funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For raw-material procurement of Lycium barbarum and herbal botanicals, settle payments below CAD 250,000 per transaction via SWIFT MT103 with invoices, packing lists, and phytosanitary certificates attached by scan. For bulk CIF/FOB orders exceeding CAD 250,000, issue an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600 confirmed by a correspondent bank in the seller's country, with a 90-120 day usance tenor and the full document package: commercial invoice, certificate of origin, phytosanitary certificate, weight list, inspection certificates, and clean bill of lading. A blended 30-50% telegraphic-transfer advance with the LC balance is the recommended clearing pattern to mitigate counterparty risk while preserving access to Canadian trade-finance facilities. Each outward remittance must reference the corresponding B13A export declaration for customs reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable FX forward of up to 24 months tenor under an ISDA master agreement with any Schedule I bank
CAD/CNY deliverable FX forward available bilaterally where the Canadian bank maintains a CNY nostro line
USD/CNY non-deliverable forward (NDF) referencing offshore CNH mid-market rates, permitted as an OTC principal-to-principal derivative without exchange clearing
Cross-currency swap (CAD/USD or CAD/CNY) for matching intercompany loan principal and interest flows
FX swap (same-day value) for temporary treasury liquidity rebalancing between USD and CAD accounts
Plain-vanilla European FX call/put options quoted in CAD/USD or USD/CNY, permissible under OSFI derivatives guidance when the notional size is below mandatory central-yield thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (annual corporate filing under the Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties escalate from CAD 50 to CAD 250; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after fiscal year-end; nine months after fiscal year-end for an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; daily interest on unpaid balances; additional penalties for gross negligence or wilful default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit for BC unlimited liability corporations under the BC Business Corporations Act. An audit is triggered if required by the articles, demanded by a shareholder under section 205, or applicable because the entity is a reporting issuer or is regulated under financial-institution legislation. CRA may also require audited financial statements where the books and records are inadequate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Private Enterprise GAAP (ASPE) is permissible for a private BC company; IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises or where shareholders elect to adopt it.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual review of the BC Transparency Register concurrent with the annual report. The register must identify every significant individual holding 25% or more of any class of shares or exercising significant control. UBO information is maintained on site and is available for inspection by the BC Corporate Registry and law enforcement; it is not filed with the government in the annual report.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Transparency Register of Significant Controlling Individuals (UBO Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable if audit-exempt; if shareholder-requested, typically $2,500 - $8,000 for a small wholesale export ULC

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% (basic 38% less 10% provincial abatement less 13% general rate reduction) plus British Columbia provincial general rate 12% = combined 27% general rate on active business income. For a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) qualifying for the Small Business Deduction (SBD), the effective combined rate is 18% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (federal 9% + BC 9%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SBD on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (phased out for taxable capital between CAD 10M and CAD 15M); BC provincial SBD at 9% on the same base; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable Investment Tax Credits of 35% for CCPCs on up to CAD 3M of eligible expenditure and 15% non-refundable otherwise; accelerated capital cost allowance under Classes 43.1/43.2 for clean-energy assets; immediate expensing under s. 1100 of the Income Tax Regulations for certain Canadian manufacturing and clean-energy equipment; foreign tax credits under s. 126 to relieve double taxation of foreign-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.loss_utilization_notes: Under s. 111(1)(a) ITA, non-capital losses (business losses) may be carried back 3 taxation years and forward 20 taxation years. Capital losses may be carried back 3 years and forward 3 years, offsetting only taxable capital gains. A BC ULC is taxed as a resident corporation in Canada and is entitled to the same loss utilization rules as any other corporation incorporated in Canada.
